Try and keep the problems in middle school math level and avoid using functions like $\Sigma$ or $\Pi$ or other functions of this sort. The problems and answers go in standard format[hide=P#]XXX[/hide]

Tony and Maria are training for a race by running all the way up and down a 700 m long ski slope. They each run up the slope at different constant speeds. Coming down the slope, each runs at double his or her uphill speed. Maria reaches the top first, and immediately starts running back down, meeting Tony 70 m from the top. topics.title: Partition function
topics.text:
I invented a new function which I named "Partition function" which I have a nice symbol to represent with but I cannot show it  here. Lets take it as $F$. It takes 2 arguments N and r (where N and r are natural numbers with $r<=N$).

$F(N,r)$ is the number ways the number N can represented as the sum of r positive integral summands i.e the number of ways we can add r positive integers to make upto N. For example $F(5,2)= 2$, as there are only two ways to represent 5 as the sum of 2 positive integers viz 1+ 4 and 2+3. Note that we cannot take 5+0, as the summands must be positive integers. Also note that 1+4 and 4+1 are taken to be the same, they are not treated as different, so the order does not matter. Now the real challenge is to find a general formula for $F(N,r)$. At first I thought it is a distribution problem where N identical balls are to be distributed among r people where each person receives at least 1 ball. But then I realized that here order matters i.e in our example 1+4 and 4+1 are taken to be different while in partion function they are the same. Any way I failed to come up with a formula but I discovered some properties shown below, which can be derived easily. So can anybody give me a generalised formula for this Partition function like we have a formula for permutation,combination and Derangement,etc?

Some properties of Partition function:-

1) $F(N,N)=1$

2)$F(N,1)=1$

3) $F(N,N-1)=1$

4) $F(N,2)= [N/2]$, where [ ] is the Greatest Integer function.

topics.text:
I just wanted to double check my answer to this problem I made. : You are going to buy a dozen donuts at a donut shop.  You can chose from 4 flavors (chocolate, lemon, jelly, and glazed). There are infinite glazed and chocolate donuts, but they only have 5 lemon left, and 3 jelly left. How many different combinations of donuts can you get?

My answer :Click to reveal hidden text346, please let me know what you got


I do not know if I am right, so please let me know.

My full answer Click to reveal hidden textP(X)=all combinations that are allowed (answer)

P(N)=total combinations with no restrictions

P(N1)=Unfavorable lemon

P(N2)=Unfavorable jelly

P(N3)=Total unfavorable



P(X)=P(N)-P(N3)

P(N3)=P(N1)+P(N2)-P(N1N2)



P(X)=(15C3) - ((9C3)+(11C3)-(5C3))

P(X)=346
